answers.implementation_then_now: On 1 Jan. 2023, practice from the period shows undocumented children being admitted to public schools. UNICEF (Dec. 2021) reports a DGME–MEP drive in which MEP referred at least 6,000 files of enrolled foreign students for regularisation; more than 8,000 applications came from minors already enrolled, many of them irregular. UNHCR's help page says refugee and asylum-seeking children enrol on the same requirements as Costa Ricans. On 1 Jan. 2026 the picture is the same: no rule change and no documented systematic exclusion. The remaining gaps are documents and certification. In May 2025 the Defensoría de los Habitantes asked the MEP to report on schooling for the deported children held at CATEM Sur (26 minors still there), which points to a gap for detained children, not to general exclusion. Usually on both dates; no shift found.

Decree 40529-MEP is at 'Versión 3 de 3', last amended 9 Jan. 2019 (Decreto 41630), so the text in force in 2023 and 2026 is the one read. Const. art. 78 was last amended by Ley 8954 (2011). Ley 7739 arts. 3, 59 and 60 and Ley 8764 art. 31 carry no amendment notes. Practice evidence for 2023–2025 on irregular children is thin; MEP enrolment statistics do not break down migration status.

answers.notes: The answer rests on statutes and regulations; no court decision is relied on. Decree 40529-MEP passages read on SCIJ: art. 5, 'Toda persona menor de edad tiene derecho a recibir educación pública gratuita. En ningún caso, el ejercicio de ese derecho estará sujeto a discriminación por su situación socioeconómica, estatus migratorio irregular...'; art. 12(f), 'el carné consular es un documento de identidad válido... Además el procedimiento de matrícula es el mismo que rige para estudiantes costarricenses.' No amendment, repeal or ruling bearing on this indicator was found between 1 Jan. 2023 and 1 Jan. 2026. Confidence is medium only because the in-window practice evidence on irregular children is thin.

events.instrument: Sala Constitucional, Sentencia N.º 2024-029734 (exp. 23-011056-0007-CO), acción de inconstitucionalidad
events.article: Art. 5, Reglamento de Adjudicación de becas a la población estudiantil de la UCR
events.what_changed: Before the ruling, UCR's scholarship rule did not cover foreigners with regular status outside the listed categories (e.g. student-category DIMEX holders). The ruling, binding erga omnes, declared that relative omission unconstitutional, so foreigners with regular migration status must be read as included. This widens equal access for regular migrants within the same middle option; irregular migrants stay outside.
events.passage: Se declara CON LUGAR la acción. En consecuencia, se declara inconstitucional la omisión relativa contenida en el artículo 5 del Reglamento de Adjudicación de becas a la población estudiantil de la Universidad de Costa Rica, en el sentido de que debe entenderse incluida la población extranjera con estatus migratorio regular en el país

events.instrument: Ley para la promoción, atracción y estadía de estudiantes, docentes e investigadores extranjeros, N.º 10645
events.what_changed: Added a migration-policy aim of streamlining procedures for foreign students, teachers and researchers. Recast special category 94(4) as 'Personas estudiantes, docentes, pasantes, investigadoras y voluntarios con fines educativos y culturales', including short stays. This eases student permits for incoming foreigners but does not change who is guaranteed access to public adult or higher education. Date is the law's date in the SCIJ note; publication and entry-into-force date not read.
events.passage: 4) Personas estudiantes, docentes, pasantes, investigadoras y voluntarios con fines educativos y culturales, incluyendo aquellos invitados, para que realicen actividades de corta estadía. (Así reformado el inciso anterior por el artículo 2° de la Ley para la promoción, atracción y estadía de estudiantes, docentes e investigadores extranjeros, N° 10645 del 24 de febrero del 2025)

answers.implementation_then_now: Around 1 Jan. 2023, the Sala Constitucional file in 2024-029734 records UCR refusing a socio-economic scholarship in 2023 to a student-category DIMEX holder because of his migration category: a status barrier for regular migrants. UNHCR's guidance shows INA requiring an asylum-seeker card, refugee DIMEX or other proof of regular status, which bars irregular migrants. By 1 Jan. 2026, UCR's rule had to be read as covering regular-status foreigners after the October 2024 ruling, and INA reported training 475 refugees in 2023–2024 (Delfino, Dec. 2024). These improvements are modest and concern regular migrants and refugees. Document and diploma-recognition barriers persist, and nothing measures labour or temporary migrants at INA. I keep 'Sometimes; Usually' on both dates: the evidence shows no shift large enough to move the rating.

answers.notes: Court decision relied on: I read judgment 2024-029734 itself, with the corrected operative part, on Nexus PJ. It is an acción de inconstitucionalidad with general effect, but confined to UCR's scholarship rule. It refines the protection for regular migrants within the same middle option. I therefore code the change as 'not the same' rather than 'no change'; the option and score are identical on both dates. The INA regulation of 7 Nov. 2023 (DIMEX/ID requirement) also falls in the window, but its text could not be opened, so it is not counted as an event. Ley 10645 touches student permits for incoming foreigners, not equal access, and its exact entry-into-force date was not read. MEP adult schooling (Decree 40529 art. 12(f)) is open regardless of status on both dates.
